docs.title: valigo
docs.text:
valigo is a validation library for Go structs. Rules are configured once, in code, by pointers to the fields of a model: b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of).Required().MaxLen(64). The compiler checks that a rule fits the field type and that its arguments have the field type, the validation itself doesn't allocate on valid objects, and error messages are translated.

One-line ideology

Rules are Go code next to the struct, not strings in tags: a typo or a wrong type doesn't compile.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
go get github.com/insei/valigo@latest

Minimum Go version is 1.27: the configurator uses generic methods.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "regexp"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/num"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type User struct {
    Name  string
    Email string
    Age   int
    Phone *string
    Tags  []string
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[User](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[User], u *User) {
        b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of).Trim().Required().MaxLen(64)
        b.Field(&u.Email).As(str.Of).Required().Email()
        b.Field(&u.Age).As(num.Of).AnyOfInterval(18, 120)
        b.Field(&u.Phone).As(str.Of).Regexp(regexp.MustCompile(`^\+\d{10,15}$`)) // a nil phone is skipped
        b.Slice(&u.Tags).As(str.Slice).MaxLen(5).Each(func(tag *str.BaseConfigurator) {
            tag.Trim().Required().MaxLen(16)
        })
    })

    user := &User{Name: "  Ann  ", Email: "ann.example.com", Age: 16, Tags: []string{"go", " "}}
    for _, err := range v.Validate(context.Background(), user) {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("%q\n", user.Name)
}

Output:

Should be email address (Email: ann.example.com)
Only interval[18 - 120] is allowed (Age: 16)
Should be fulfilled (Tags[1]: )
"Ann"

What happens here:

  1. valigo.New() creates a validator with the messages in English, German, Spanish, French and Russian.
  2. valigo.Configure[User] calls the function once with a model: a *User whose nested pointer structs are allocated. Rules are bound to the fields of the model by their pointers, &u.Name.
  3. Every configurator method returns the configurator of the field, so rules are chained. They run in the order of the chain: Trim changes the value before Required checks it.
  4. v.Validate runs the rules of the *User type and returns nil for a valid object. Every error has the message, the location of the field (Tags[1] for the element of a slice) and the value.

docs.title: For AI agents
docs.text: AI agents often write the code that uses a library, and a model trained before the typed configurator doesn't know its API: it writes b.String(&u.Name) of the old API instead of b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of), or Max(int64(5)) with an any argument. Give the agent the current documentation.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
The bench module compares valigo with go-playground/validator, ozzo-validation, zog, gookit/validate and hand-written Go code on the same struct and the same rules: a required name up to 64 characters, a required email, an age in [18, 120], up to 5 required tags up to 16 characters and a required city of a nested struct. A test checks that the libraries find the same errors.

b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of).Required().MaxRunes(64)
b.Field(&u.Email).As(str.Of).Required().Email()
b.Field(&u.Age).As(num.Of).AnyOfInterval(18, 120)
b.Slice(&u.Tags).As(str.Slice).MaxLen(5).Each(func(tag *str.BaseConfigurator) { tag.Required().MaxRunes(16) })
b.Field(&u.Address.City).As(str.Of).Required()

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Intel Core i9-14900HX, Go 1.27.0, one CPU (-cpu 1), the median of 6 runs.

A valid object:

Library ns/op B/op allocs/op hand-written code, the lower bound 286 0 0 valigo 407 0 0 zog 1 690 6 2 go-playground/validator 1 785 296 16 ozzo-validation 2 950 2 000 38 gookit/validate 6 880 4 560 65

An invalid object with 6 errors:

Library ns/op B/op allocs/op hand-written code, errors without messages 590 288 8 valigo, translated messages 2 205 1 168 14 go-playground/validator, without messages 2 665 1 688 45 go-playground/validator, with Error() of every error 4 150 2 488 69 zog, issues with messages 4 600 1 056 24 ozzo-validation, with Error() 12 665 11 026 140 gookit/validate 13 250 9 569 120

valigo is about 1.4 times slower than the same rules written by hand on a valid object, it pays for the closures of the rules; it doesn't allocate either. The fields are read by the offsets of fmap without reflect, following the pointers of nested structs. Code generators of validators produce code like the hand-written one, so they are expected to be about as fast as it.

  • valigo builds the rules once in Configure and reads the fields by precomputed accessors, so valid objects cost no allocations; go-playground/validator parses the tags once too, but works through reflect on every call, ozzo-validation builds its rules on every call of Validate.
  • gookit/validate creates a validation per call, it is its API, and reports the errors of the elements of a slice under one key Tags.*; zog builds the messages of its issues.
  • valigo builds the translated messages of the errors at once, go-playground/validator returns the errors without messages and builds them by Error or Translate: compare valigo with the row "with Error()".
  • The rules of valigo append the errors to one pooled buffer, Validate copies it once; most allocations of an invalid object are the messages and the boxed values of the errors.

docs.title: Upgrading from v0.0.x
docs.text:
Rules are still configured by pointers to the fields of the model, but the configurator is typed now and knows nothing about the types of the values: a field is converted to the configurator of its type by As. Go 1.27 is required.

v0.0.x Now b.String(&u.Name) b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of) b.Number(&u.Age) b.Field(&u.Age).As(num.Of) b.Number(&u.Score) for *int b.Field(&u.Score).As(num.Ptr) b.UUID(&u.ID) b.Field(&u.ID).As(vuuid.Of) of the separate module github.com/insei/valigo/uuid b.StringSlice(&u.Tags) b.Slice(&u.Tags).As(str.Slice), for *[]string: b.Field(&u.Tags).As(shared.SlicePtr).As(str.Slice) b.UUIDSlice(&u.IDs) b.Slice(&u.IDs).As(vuuid.Slice) b.Slice(any) with Custom(func(ctx, h, value []*any) ...) b.Slice(&u.Items) with Custom(func(ctx, h, value shared.Elems[E]) ...) and Each Configurator[T] is an interface a struct with generic methods, the signature of the Configure function is the same field configurators are interfaces: str.BaseConfigurator, num.BaseConfigurator pointers to concrete types: *str.BaseConfigurator, *num.BaseConfigurator[N], *vuuid.BaseConfigurator Max(any), Min(any), AnyOf(...any), AnyOfInterval(any, any) the arguments have the type of the field, Max(5) works for int64 Custom(func(ctx, h, value any) ...), When(func(ctx, value any) bool) of fields the value is typed: string, the number type, uuid.UUID StringSlice(...).MaxLen(n) the same: the number of elements; rules on elements are set by Each shared.NewSliceFieldConfigurator(params), shared.FieldConfigurator shared.NewSliceFieldConfigurator(field, helper, add), shared.Field[T]

docs.title: Behavior changes
docs.text:
• Validate returns nil for a valid object, it returned an empty slice. Check len(errs) > 0 or errs != nil, both work now.
  • A struct value is validated by a copy, it was silently skipped.
  • Nil pointers and the fields of nil nested structs are skipped by rules, they panicked; Required fails on them.
  • Required of num.Of fails on zero, it did nothing. Required of num.Ptr fails on nil.
  • AnyOfInterval(begin, end) includes both ends.
  • The errors of slice elements have the index in the location: Tags[1].
  • A field When isn't called for an absent value, it got the zero value.
  • A repeated Configure of the same type replaces its rules, it appended them.
  • shared.Error has Code and Params, its JSON has them when they aren't empty; the messages of counts have plural forms: "longer than 1 character".

docs.title: Why valigo?
docs.text: valigo is for Go services that validate their input structs and want the rules checked by the compiler, the validation free on valid input, and the messages in the language of the user.

docs.title: Rules are code, checked by the compiler
docs.text:
Rules are configured by pointers to the fields of the model, so the field and its type are known at compile time. As converts the field to the configurator of its type, and the conversion has a type constraint:

b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of).Required().MaxLen(64) // str.Of accepts string, *string and named strings
b.Field(&u.ID).As(num.Of).Min(1)                  // Min takes an int64 for an int64 field
b.Field(&u.ID).As(num.Of).Min("1")                // doesn't compile
b.Field(&u.Age).As(str.Of)                        // doesn't compile: int does not satisfy ~string | *string

A renamed field is renamed in the rules by the IDE, a removed field breaks the build instead of a silently skipped rule. Tag based validators keep the rules in strings, validate:"required,max=64", and report a typo or a rule of a wrong type only at runtime.

docs.title: Any type, without changes of the library
docs.text: The configurator knows nothing about strings, numbers or uuids: they are conversions in their packages. A type of your domain, time.Time or a uuid of another package gets its rules by a conversion function of a few lines, see Types and conversions.

docs.title: Validation of valid objects doesn't allocate
docs.text: The rules are built once by Configure. Validate reads the fields through precomputed accessors and calls the rules of every field, allocations happen only to build errors. A struct with string, number, uuid and slice rules, conditions and a struct level custom rule is validated with 0 allocations — the tests check it. On the same rules a valid object is validated about 4 times faster than by go-playground/validator and 1.4 times slower than by the same rules written by hand, an invalid one with translated messages — about 2 times faster than go-playground/validator builds its messages, see Performance.

docs.title: Absent values are handled, not panicked on
docs.text:
A nil pointer field, a nil pointer to a slice and the fields of a nil nested struct are absent: every rule skips them, only Required fails. Optional fields need no special code:

b.Field(&u.Phone).As(str.Of).Regexp(phoneRe)    // nil Phone is valid, a set one must match
b.Field(&u.Discount).As(num.Ptr).Max(50)         // nil Discount is valid
b.Field(&u.Address.City).As(str.Of).Required()  // fails for a nil Address too

docs.title: Conditions and custom rules at every level
docs.text:
When on the struct enables rules by the state of the object, When on a field — by the value of the field. Custom on a field gets its typed value, Custom on the struct gets the whole object and reports errors on any of its fields:

smtp := b.When(func(_ context.Context, s *Sender) bool { return s.Type == "smtp" })
smtp.Field(&s.Host).As(str.Of).Required()
smtp.Field(&s.Port).As(num.Of).AnyOfInterval(1, 65535)

See Conditions and Custom rules.

docs.title: Messages in the language of the user, or codes for the client
docs.text:
One validator serves all languages: the language of every request comes from the context, NewAcceptLanguageMiddleware puts the languages of the Accept-Language header there. The messages of the built-in rules are translated to English, German, Spanish, French and Russian with plural forms, your own messages are added to the same storage and work untranslated until you add translations. A client with its own locales gets a stable Code and named Params of every error instead. See Translations and Codes for clients.

How the libraries compare, by their documentation:

valigo go-playground/validator ozzo-validation Translations out of the box en, de, es, fr, ru many languages, the packages of validator/translations English messages Language of a request from the context, one validator for all languages a translator of universal-translator is picked and passed to Translate for every request the messages are global Setup none, valigo.New() a translator per language and the registration of the translations of every tag replacing the message templates of the errors Plural forms CLDR categories in the locale files cardinal rules of universal-translator — Codes for clients Code and named Params of every error the tag and one string parameter of a field error the code and the parameters of an error Messages of own rules the message is its locale key, translated when a translation is added a translation is registered for every tag the message of the error

docs.title: Slices, maps and other fields
docs.text: The rules of a slice check the slice itself and, by Each, every element with the rules of its type; maps have EachKey and EachValue; a rule can compare a field with another one by its pointer — b.Field(&o.EndsAt).As(timex.Of).AfterField(&o.StartsAt) — with the type of the other field checked by the compiler. See Slices, Maps and Rules on other fields.

docs.title: Ready for HTTP APIs
docs.text: The problem package writes the errors as application/problem+json of RFC 9457 with JSON pointers to the fields, the github.com/insei/valigo/huma module puts the rules into the inputs of huma operations with the locations of huma. See HTTP problem details and huma.

docs.title: Errors that point to the field
docs.text: Every error has the message, the location and the value: Tags[1] for an element of a slice, Address.City for a nested field, or the JSON path of the field with a custom location function. See Errors.

docs.title: When valigo is not the right tool
docs.text:
• The fields aren't known at compile time, e.g. a form builder with fields defined by users: valigo validates the fields of Go structs. The limits and the conditions of the rules can come from the data — a database, a cache, the settings of a tenant — see Rules from data.
  • The input is not a struct: valigo validates structs, decode maps and JSON into a struct first.
  • Go older than 1.27: the configurator uses generic methods.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: This page is for the contributors and for those who want to know the cost of a rule.

docs.title: Configure: from pointers to fields
docs.text:
Configure[T] creates the model, a *T with all exported nested structs stored by pointer allocated (pointers to the types being allocated are left nil, so recursive types stop). The model gives every field a unique address, so a pointer &u.Address.City identifies the field: fmap finds the field descriptor by the address relative to the model.

The descriptor knows the offset of the field and the chain of the nested pointer structs, so it reads the field of any object of the type: Address.City of a *User follows the Address pointer and returns a typed nil pointer when it is nil. That's how absent values appear.

docs.title: Typed rules
docs.text:
The configurator methods are generic: Field[F any](p *F) *shared.Field[F], Slice[E any](p *[]E). The type of the field becomes the type parameter of the base configurator. As is a generic method too, it takes a conversion with a type constraint, str.Of[S ~string | *string](f *shared.Field[S]): the compiler checks the constraint against the type of the field, and the conversion fixes the types of the rule arguments.

Every typed configurator is a thin wrapper over one core type, shared.Field[T]. It has four primitives, all built-in rules are made of them:

Primitive Behavior Check(ok, key, args...) an error with the key when ok(value) is false, absent values are skipped Required(ok, key) an error when the value is absent or ok(value) is false Modify(fn) changes the value in place, e.g. Trim Custom(fn) your function with the typed value and the field helper

When(cond) wraps the next rules of the field with the condition. MaxLen of a string is Check(func(v string) bool { return len(v) <= n }, ...).

shared.Field[T] doesn't know where the value comes from. For a struct field the source reads the field, for Each the source iterates over the elements of the slice and adds the index to the locations of the errors, for the keys and the values of a map it copies them to a pooled slot. All rules of a source share one read of the value. That's why the same string configurator validates a Name string field and every element of Tags []*string.

docs.title: Validate: the hot path
docs.text:
Configure registers one validation function per field source in the validator, keyed by the type *T. Validate:

  1. finds the functions of the type of the object, a map lookup;
  2. calls every function: it reads the field once through the descriptor, a pointer into the object, and runs the rules of the field;
  3. a rule returns nil for a valid value, and builds a shared.Error with the translated message otherwise.

Nothing in this path allocates for valid objects: the values are read by pointers, the rules are closures created by Configure, the regexps are compiled once, the messages and their parameters are built by shared.M on the configuration, and the helper of struct Custom rules is pooled. A test of every package checks it with testing.AllocsPerRun.

The rules append their errors to one pooled buffer of the validation, and Validate copies it once: an invalid object allocates the copy, the translated messages and the boxed values of its errors.

docs.title: Absent values
docs.text:
A value is absent when there is nothing to check:

  • a nil pointer field: *string, *int, *uuid.UUID;
  • a nil pointer to a slice: *[]string;
  • a field of a nested struct stored by a nil pointer: City of a nil *Address;
  • a nil element of a slice of pointers: []*string{nil}.

Every rule skips absent values, only Required fails on them. So an optional field needs no special code: the rules check it only when it is set.

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/num"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type Address struct {
    City string
}

type Order struct {
    Comment  *string
    Discount *int
    Coupons  *[]string
    Delivery *Address
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Order](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Order], o *Order) {
        b.Field(&o.Comment).As(str.Of).MaxLen(200)
        b.Field(&o.Discount).As(num.Ptr).AnyOfInterval(1, 50)
        b.Field(&o.Coupons).As(shared.SlicePtr).As(str.Slice).MaxLen(3)
        b.Field(&o.Delivery.City).As(str.Of).Required()
    })

    // nothing is set: only the Required rule fails
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Order{}))

    discount := 70
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Order{Discount: &discount, Delivery: &Address{City: "Paris"}}))
}

Output:

[Should be fulfilled (Delivery.City: <nil>)]
[Only interval[1 - 50] is allowed (Discount: 70)]

docs.title: Required
docs.text:
What Required checks depends on the type:

Conversion Fails on str.Of absent value, empty string num.Of zero num.Ptr absent value; zero is a valid value of a pointer uuid.Of absent value, uuid.Nil Slice, str.Slice, uuid.Slice absent slice, empty slice

Nil slices of value fields ([]string(nil)) are present and empty: length rules check them, Each has nothing to check.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text: A field When doesn't call its condition for an absent value and skips its rules, including Required: the condition is about the value, and there is no value. Put Required before When, or use When of the struct, if the field is required under a condition. See Conditions.

docs.title: When on the struct
docs.text:
When of the configurator returns a configurator whose rules are applied only if the function returns true for the validated object:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/num"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type Sender struct {
    Type     string
    SMTPHost string
    SMTPPort int
    HTTPURL  string
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Sender](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Sender], s *Sender) {
        b.Field(&s.Type).As(str.Of).AnyOf("smtp", "http")

        smtp := b.When(func(_ context.Context, s *Sender) bool { return s.Type == "smtp" })
        smtp.Field(&s.SMTPHost).As(str.Of).Required()
        smtp.Field(&s.SMTPPort).As(num.Of).AnyOfInterval(1, 65535)

        http := b.When(func(_ context.Context, s *Sender) bool { return s.Type == "http" })
        http.Field(&s.HTTPURL).As(str.Of).Required()
    })

    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Sender{Type: "smtp"}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Sender{Type: "http"}))
}

Output:

[Should be fulfilled (SMTPHost: ) Only interval[1 - 65535] is allowed (SMTPPort: 0)]
[Should be fulfilled (HTTPURL: )]
  • The returned configurator has all methods of the original one, the conditions of chained When calls are combined with AND: b.When(a).When(b).
  • When doesn't change the configurator it is called on: b keeps adding unconditional rules.
  • The context passed to Validate is passed to the condition, e.g. to enable rules by the role of the user.

docs.title: When on a field
docs.text:
When of a field configurator returns a configurator of the same field whose rules are applied only if the function returns true for the value of the field. The rules before When stay unconditional:

b.Field(&u.Website).As(str.Of).
    Trim().                                                                  // always
    When(func(_ context.Context, v string) bool { return v != "" }).
    Regexp(urlRe)                                                            // only for a non-empty value

The value is typed: string for str.Of, the number type for num.Of and num.Ptr, uuid.UUID for uuid.Of, and shared.Elems[E] for slices, see Slices.

For an absent value the condition isn't called and the rules after it are skipped, including Required.

docs.title: Conditional requiredness
docs.text:
Tag based validators have families of tags like required_if, required_with and required_without. In valigo they are When with a condition on the fields:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type Customer struct {
    Kind    string
    TaxID   string
    Phone   string
    Email   string
    Company string
    Title   string
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Customer](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Customer], c *Customer) {
        // required_if=Kind company
        b.When(func(_ context.Context, c *Customer) bool { return c.Kind == "company" }).Field(&c.TaxID).As(str.Of).Required()
        // required_without=Email: a phone or an email
        b.When(func(_ context.Context, c *Customer) bool { return c.Email == "" }).Field(&c.Phone).As(str.Of).Required()
        // required_with=Company: the title of the person in the company
        b.When(func(_ context.Context, c *Customer) bool { return c.Company != "" }).Field(&c.Title).As(str.Of).Required()
        // excluded_unless=Kind company
        b.When(func(_ context.Context, c *Customer) bool { return c.Kind != "company" }).Field(&c.Company).As(str.Of).
            Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, company string) []shared.Error {
                if company != "" {
                    return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, company, "Only companies have a company")}
                }
                return nil
            })
    })

    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Customer{Kind: "company"}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Customer{Kind: "person", Email: "a@b.cc", Company: "ACME"}))
}

Output:

[Should be fulfilled (TaxID: ) Should be fulfilled (Phone: )]
[Should be fulfilled (Title: ) Only companies have a company (Company: ACME)]

docs.title: Conditions and custom rules
docs.text: A condition on several fields can also be written as a struct custom rule, which reports errors itself. Prefer When: the rules after it are the regular ones, with their messages and translations.

docs.title: Validator
docs.text:
valigo.New creates a validator. It holds the rules of all configured types and the translator of the messages, create one per application and share it.

v := valigo.New(
    valigo.WithTranslator(t),                     // translator of the messages, see Translations
    valigo.WithFieldLocationNamingFn(jsonPath),   // location of the field in errors, see Errors
    valigo.WithErrorsTransformer(toProblemFields), // []shared.Error to []error for Validate, see Errors
)

All options are optional, a nil argument keeps the default.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
valigo.Configure[T] configures the rules of the struct type T:

valigo.Configure[User](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[User], u *User) {
    b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of).Required()
})

The function is called once, with:

  • b — the configurator of T: Field, Slice and Map return the base configurators of fields, converted to the configurators of their types by As, see Types and conversions; When and Custom are the rules of the struct;
  • u — the model, a *User created by Configure. Rules are bound to the fields of the model by their pointers.

The rules are applied to objects of type *T: v.Validate(ctx, &user). A struct value is validated too, by a copy, see Errors.

Configure is called on the application start. It isn't safe to call concurrently with Validate, and it panics on invalid configuration: a configuration error is a bug of the code, not a state of the running service. A repeated Configure of the same type replaces its rules.

docs.title: Field pointers
docs.text:
A field pointer must point to a field of the model passed to the function:

valigo.Configure[User](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[User], u *User) {
    b.Field(&u.Name)         // a field of the model
    b.Field(&u.Address.City) // a field of a nested struct of the model

    var name string
    b.Field(&name)           // panic: *string is not a pointer to a field of *main.User: field not found
})

Types of the fields are checked by the compiler: b.Field(&u.Age).As(str.Of) doesn't compile for an int field, the conversions accept only the types they support.

docs.title: Nested structs
docs.text:
Fields of nested structs are configured by the same pointers. The model allocates all nested structs stored by pointer, so &u.Address.City is valid even if Address is *Address:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type Address struct {
    City string
}

type User struct {
    Name    string
    Home    Address
    Work    *Address
    Manager *User // recursive types are supported, the model doesn't allocate Manager
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[User](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[User], u *User) {
        b.Field(&u.Home.City).As(str.Of).Required()
        b.Field(&u.Work.City).As(str.Of).Required()
    })

    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &User{Work: &Address{}}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &User{Home: Address{City: "Berlin"}}))
}

Output:

[Should be fulfilled (Home.City: ) Should be fulfilled (Work.City: )]
[Should be fulfilled (Work.City: <nil>)]

When the validated object has a nil Work, the field Work.City is absent: rules skip it and Required fails, see Absent values.

Embedded structs work the same way, &u.ID for a field of an embedded Base. Unexported fields are allowed in the model, and unexported fields of the model itself can be configured too.

docs.title: Reusing rules
docs.text:
Rules of nested types aren't inherited: configuring Address doesn't add its rules to User. Share the rules by a function:

func addressRules[T any](b valigo.Configurator[T], a *Address) {
    b.Field(&a.City).As(str.Of).Required()
}

valigo.Configure[User](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[User], u *User) {
    addressRules(b, &u.Home)
    addressRules(b, u.Work)
})

docs.title: Types and conversions
docs.text:
The configurator knows nothing about the types of the values. It has two methods for the fields:

  • b.Field(&m.X) returns *shared.Field[T], the base configurator of a field of type T;
  • b.Slice(&m.X) returns *shared.SliceFieldConfigurator[E] of a []E field, with the rules of the slice itself: Required, MinLen, MaxLen, Custom, When and Each;
  • b.Map(&m.X) returns *shared.MapFieldConfigurator[K, V] of a map[K]V field, with the rules of the map itself, EachKey and EachValue, see Maps.

As converts a base configurator to the configurator of its type. A conversion is a function with a type constraint, so a conversion that doesn't fit the field doesn't compile:

b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of).Required()       // string
b.Field(&u.Discount).As(num.Ptr).Max(50)     // *int
b.Slice(&u.Tags).MaxLen(5).As(str.Slice).Email()

b.Field(&u.Age).As(str.Of)
// int does not satisfy ~string | *string (int missing in ~string | *string)

docs.title: Built-in conversions
docs.text:
Conversion Fields Configurator str.Of string, *string, named strings strings num.Of numbers and named numbers numbers num.Slice Slice of numbers slices with the number rules of elements num.Ptr pointers to numbers numbers, Required checks only that the pointer isn't nil timex.Of time.Time, *time.Time time eq.Of, eq.Ptr any comparable type and pointers to it: enums, bool comparable values vuuid.Of uuid.UUID, *uuid.UUID of github.com/google/uuid uuid, the separate module github.com/insei/valigo/uuid str.Slice Slice of strings, *string or named strings slices with the string rules of elements timex.Slice Slice of time.Time, *time.Time slices with the time rules of elements eq.Slice Slice of a comparable type slices with Unique and the equality rules of elements vuuid.Slice Slice of uuid.UUID, *uuid.UUID slices with the uuid rules of elements shared.SlicePtr Field of *[]E the slice configurator, a nil pointer is absent

The elements of a slice are converted in Each: b.Slice(&m.Sizes).Each(func(e *shared.Field[int]) { e.As(num.Of).Min(1) }).

docs.title: The base rules
docs.text:
shared.Field[T] has the primitives all configurators are built of. They are enough for a one-off rule without a conversion:

Rule Behavior Check(ok, key, args...) an error with the message key when ok(value) is false, absent values are skipped Required(ok, key) an error when the value is absent or ok(value) is false Modify(fn) changes the value in place, e.g. trims it Custom(fn) your function with the typed value, see Custom rules When(cond) the next rules are applied only if cond(value) is true, see Conditions 
b.Field(&o.Paid).Check(func(paid bool) bool { return paid }, "Should be paid")

docs.title: Your types
docs.text:
A conversion of your type is a function that takes the base configurator and returns your configurator over shared.Field of the type. Use the conversions of shared for pointers and named types:

  • shared.Deref converts the rules of *T to the rules of T, a nil pointer is absent;
  • shared.Retype converts the rules of T to the rules of U with the same memory layout, e.g. of a named type;
  • shared.RetypeSlice does the same for a slice configurator, also for the elements stored by pointer;
  • shared.SliceRules gives Required, MinLen, MaxLen, Custom and When of the slice to your slice configurator, see the source of str.Slice;
  • CheckMsg and RequiredMsg take a message of shared.M with a stable code and named parameters: c.f.CheckMsg(ok, shared.M("time.after", key, shared.P("time", t))).

A configurator of time.Time (the built-in one is timex, this one shows how it's made):

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "time"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
)

// TimeConfigurator configures the rules of a time.Time value.
type TimeConfigurator struct {
    f *shared.Field[time.Time]
}

// TimeOf converts a time.Time or *time.Time field: b.Field(&m.At).As(TimeOf).
func TimeOf[T time.Time | *time.Time](f *shared.Field[T]) *TimeConfigurator {
    if p, ok := any(f).(*shared.Field[*time.Time]); ok {
        return &TimeConfigurator{f: shared.Deref(p)}
    }
    return &TimeConfigurator{f: shared.Retype[T, time.Time](f)}
}

func (c *TimeConfigurator) Required() *TimeConfigurator {
    c.f.Required(func(v time.Time) bool { return !v.IsZero() }, "Should be fulfilled")
    return c
}

func (c *TimeConfigurator) After(t time.Time) *TimeConfigurator {
    c.f.Check(func(v time.Time) bool { return v.After(t) }, "Should be after %s", t.Format(time.DateOnly))
    return c
}

type Event struct {
    StartsAt time.Time
    EndsAt   *time.Time
}

func main() {
    start := time.Date(2026, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Event](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Event], e *Event) {
        b.Field(&e.StartsAt).As(TimeOf).Required().After(start)
        b.Field(&e.EndsAt).As(TimeOf).After(start) // a nil EndsAt is skipped
    })

    before := start.AddDate(0, 0, -1)
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Event{}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Event{StartsAt: start.AddDate(0, 1, 0), EndsAt: &before}))
}

Output:

[Should be fulfilled (StartsAt: 0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC) Should be after 2026-01-01 (StartsAt: 0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC)]
[Should be after 2026-01-01 (EndsAt: 2025-12-31 00:00:00 +0000 UTC)]

The type constraint of TimeOf makes b.Field(&e.Title).As(TimeOf) a compile error for a string field. The rules of another uuid package are added the same way, see the source of github.com/insei/valigo/uuid.

docs.title: Field rules
docs.text:
Custom of a field configurator adds a rule with your logic. The function gets the typed value of the field and a helper that builds errors with the location of the field:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "strings"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/num"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type Account struct {
    Login string
    Age   int
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Account](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Account], a *Account) {
        b.Field(&a.Login).As(str.Of).Required().Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, login string) []shared.Error {
            if strings.EqualFold(login, "admin") {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, login, "Login %q is reserved", login)}
            }
            return nil
        })
        b.Field(&a.Age).As(num.Of).Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, age int) []shared.Error {
            if age%2 != 0 {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, age, "Should be even")}
            }
            return nil
        })
    })

    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Account{Login: "Admin", Age: 3}))
}

Output:

[Login "Admin" is reserved (Login: Admin) Should be even (Age: 3)]

h.ErrorT(ctx, value, localeKey, args...) translates the message: localeKey is looked up in the translations, a key without a translation is used as is, as a format for args. The code of the error is the key. For a stable code and named parameters build the message by shared.M and return h.ErrorMsg(ctx, value, msg):

return []shared.Error{h.ErrorMsg(ctx, login, shared.M("login.reserved", "Login %q is reserved", shared.P("login", login)))}

The values of shared.P are the format arguments of the message in their order. A message without the checked value can be created once on the configuration, its parameters are shared by the errors.

The function isn't called for an absent value.

docs.title: Rules on slice elements
docs.text:
The Each of Slice gives a *shared.Field[E] of the elements. Besides Custom and When it has Check, the base of all built-in rules: a predicate and a message for the elements that don't match it.

b.Slice(&o.Quantities).Each(func(q *shared.Field[int]) {
    q.Check(func(v int) bool { return v > 0 }, "Should be positive")
})

Required(ok, localeKey) fails for absent elements and the elements that don't match ok, Modify(fn) changes the elements in place. See Slices.

docs.title: Struct rules
docs.text:
Custom of the struct configurator gets the whole object, for the rules on several fields. h.ErrorT takes the pointer to the field of the validated object to build its location:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "time"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
)

type Booking struct {
    From time.Time
    To   time.Time
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Booking](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Booking], _ *Booking) {
        b.Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h shared.StructCustomHelper, obj *Booking) []shared.Error {
            if !obj.To.After(obj.From) {
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, &obj.To, obj.To.Format(time.DateOnly), "Should be after %s", obj.From.Format(time.DateOnly))}
            }
            return nil
        })
    })

    from := time.Date(2026, 5, 10, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &Booking{From: from, To: from.AddDate(0, 0, -1)}))
}

Output:

[Should be after 2026-05-10 (To: 2026-05-09)]
  • Struct Custom can be combined with When: b.When(cond).Custom(fn).
  • The helper is valid only during the call of the function, don't keep it.
  • A pointer that doesn't point to a field of the validated object panics.

docs.title: Rules from data
docs.text:
The rules are configured once, but they don't have to be constant: a Custom rule is a closure, it can read its limits from a database, a cache or the settings of a tenant on every validation, and it gets the context of the request. A When condition can do the same. Use the built-in message keys and codes, and the errors are translated and coded like the built-in ones:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "unicode/utf8"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type tenantKey struct{}

// Limits are the settings of the tenants, a database or a cache in a real service.
type Limits map[string]int

func (l Limits) MaxTitle(ctx context.Context) int {
    tenant, _ := ctx.Value(tenantKey{}).(string)
    return l[tenant]
}

type Post struct {
    Title string
}

func main() {
    limits := Limits{"free": 10, "pro": 100}

    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Post](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Post], p *Post) {
        b.Field(&p.Title).As(str.Of).Required().Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, title string) []shared.Error {
            if maxLen := limits.MaxTitle(ctx); utf8.RuneCountInString(title) > maxLen {
                msg := shared.M("string.max_runes", "validation:string:Cannot be longer than %d characters", shared.P("max", maxLen))
                return []shared.Error{h.ErrorMsg(ctx, title, msg)}
            }
            return nil
        })
    })

    post := &Post{Title: "Rules from the data"}
    free := context.WithValue(context.Background(), tenantKey{}, "free")
    pro := context.WithValue(context.Background(), tenantKey{}, "pro")
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(free, post))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(pro, post))
}

Output:

[Cannot be longer than 10 characters (Title: Rules from the data)]
[]

The message of the error is translated by the plural forms of the built-in key, and the client gets the code string.max_runes with the max of the tenant.

The module examples/limits is a fuller example: the limits of a title and of the number of tags by the plan of the tenant from a store that changes at runtime, and the rules of a field enabled by a feature flag.

docs.title: echo
docs.text:
The module github.com/insei/valigo/echo validates the requests of echo by valigo.

go get github.com/insei/valigo/echo@latest
  • vecho.New(v) is the echo.Validator: set e.Validator = vecho.New(v), and c.Validate(&req) validates by the rules of valigo.
  • echo doesn't pass the request to its validator, so these messages are in the default language. vecho.Validate(c, v, &req) validates with the languages of the Accept-Language header of the request.
  • The error is shared.Errors, get the errors by errors.As and write them, e.g. as problem details.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "errors"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "net/http/httptest"
    "strings"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    vecho "github.com/insei/valigo/echo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
    "github.com/labstack/echo/v4"
)

type SignUp struct {
    Email string `json:"email"`
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[SignUp](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[SignUp], s *SignUp) {
        b.Field(&s.Email).As(str.Of).Required().Email()
    })

    e := echo.New()
    e.Validator = vecho.New(v)
    e.POST("/sign-up", func(c echo.Context) error {
        var req SignUp
        if err := c.Bind(&req); err != nil {
            return err
        }
        if err := c.Validate(&req); err != nil {
            var errs shared.Errors
            if errors.As(err, &errs) {
                return c.JSON(http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, errs)
            }
            return err
        }
        return c.NoContent(http.StatusCreated)
    })

    req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/sign-up", strings.NewReader(`{"email": "ann"}`))
    req.Header.Set(echo.HeaderContentType, echo.MIMEApplicationJSON)
    w := httptest.NewRecorder()
    e.ServeHTTP(w, req)
    fmt.Println(w.Code)
    fmt.Print(w.Body.String())
}

Output:

422
[{"Message":"Should be email address","Location":"Email","Value":"ann","Code":"string.email"}]

docs.title: Validate and ValidateTyped
docs.text:
func (v *Validator) Validate(ctx context.Context, obj any) []error
func (v *Validator) ValidateTyped(ctx context.Context, obj any) []shared.Error
  • ValidateTyped returns the errors as shared.Error values, Validate passes them through the errors transformer, by default every shared.Error becomes an error.
  • Both return nil when the object is valid, when the type of the object has no rules, and for a nil pointer.
  • obj is a pointer to the configured struct. A struct value is validated too, by a shallow copy: Trim of its fields isn't visible to the caller, but the values behind its pointers and the elements of its slices are shared with the caller and can be changed.
  • The errors go in the order of the configuration: the rules of a field in the order of the chain, the fields in the order of their first rule.

docs.title: shared.Error
docs.text:
type Error struct {
    Message  string         // translated message
    Location string         // location of the field, Address.City or Tags[1] by default
    Value    any            // the checked value, nil for absent values
    Code     string         // stable code of the rule, e.g. string.max_len
    Params   map[string]any // named parameters of the message, e.g. {"max": 64}
}

Error() returns Message (Location: Value), or Message alone when both the location and the value are empty. Error has JSON field names of its own: {"Message":"...","Location":"...","Value":...,"Code":"...","Params":{...}}, Code and Params are omitted when empty. Convert it to your API format by the transformer.

docs.title: Codes for clients
docs.text:
The message is translated on the backend, see Translations. A client that translates the messages itself — a web or a mobile application with its own locales — uses Code and Params instead: the code is stable, the parameters are named.

package main

import (
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "time"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/num"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/timex"
)

type Event struct {
    Title    string
    Seats    int
    StartsAt time.Time
    EndsAt   time.Time
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Event](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Event], e *Event) {
        b.Field(&e.Title).As(str.Of).MaxLen(5)
        b.Field(&e.Seats).As(num.Of).AnyOfInterval(1, 100)
        b.Field(&e.EndsAt).As(timex.Of).AfterField(&e.StartsAt)
    })

    start := time.Date(2026, 5, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
    for _, err := range v.ValidateTyped(context.Background(), &Event{Title: "Conference", StartsAt: start, EndsAt: start}) {
        body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"field": err.Location, "code": err.Code, "params": err.Params})
        fmt.Println(string(body))
    }
}

Output:

{"code":"string.max_len","field":"Title","params":{"max":5}}
{"code":"number.interval","field":"Seats","params":{"max":100,"min":1}}
{"code":"time.after_field","field":"EndsAt","params":{"field":"StartsAt"}}

The field parameter is the location of the other field by the location function of the validator. The errors of custom rules have the locale key as the code, or the code of shared.M with ErrorMsg.

docs.title: Location of fields
docs.text:
The location is the path of the field in the struct by default: Address.City. WithFieldLocationNamingFn replaces it, e.g. with the path of the JSON tags, so the client sees the names of its request:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/fmap/v3"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type Address struct {
    City string `json:"city"`
}

type SignUp struct {
    Email   string   `json:"email"`
    Address Address  `json:"address"`
    Tags    []string `json:"tags"`
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New(valigo.WithFieldLocationNamingFn(func(field fmap.Field) string {
        return field.GetTagPath("json", false)
    }))
    valigo.Configure[SignUp](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[SignUp], s *SignUp) {
        b.Field(&s.Email).As(str.Of).Email()
        b.Field(&s.Address.City).As(str.Of).Required()
        b.Slice(&s.Tags).As(str.Slice).Email()
    })

    for _, err := range v.ValidateTyped(context.Background(), &SignUp{Email: "a", Tags: []string{"b"}}) {
        fmt.Println(err.Location, err.Message)
    }
}

Output:

email Should be email address
address.city Should be fulfilled
tags[0] Should be email address

The index of a slice element is appended to the location returned by the function.

docs.title: Errors transformer
docs.text:
WithErrorsTransformer sets how Validate converts the errors, e.g. to one error of the API:

type FieldError struct {
    Field   string `json:"field"`
    Message string `json:"message"`
}

type ValidationError struct {
    Fields []FieldError `json:"fields"`
}

func (e *ValidationError) Error() string { return "validation failed" }

v := valigo.New(valigo.WithErrorsTransformer(func(errs []shared.Error) []error {
    fields := make([]FieldError, len(errs))
    for i, err := range errs {
        fields[i] = FieldError{Field: err.Location, Message: err.Message}
    }
    return []error{&ValidationError{Fields: fields}}
}))

shared.Errors is a []shared.Error as one error, its Error() joins the errors by ;; the adapters of the frameworks return it, get it back by errors.As(err, &errs).

The transformer is called only when there are errors. For an HTTP API the problem package has the transformer of the problem details of RFC 9457.

docs.title: Rules on other fields
docs.text:
A rule can compare the value with the value of another field of the same object. The other field is passed by its pointer to the model, like the field itself, so its type is checked by the compiler and a pointer that isn't a field of the model panics in Configure:

b.Field(&o.EndsAt).As(timex.Of).AfterField(&o.StartsAt)
b.Field(&o.Price).As(num.Of).MinField(&o.MinPrice).MaxField(&o.MaxPrice)
b.Field(&u.Confirmation).As(str.Of).EqualField(&u.Password)
b.Field(&u.Plan).As(eq.Of).EqualField(&u.CurrentPlan)
Configurator Rule Fails when Message strings EqualField(&m.X) the value isn't equal to X Should be equal to %s numbers MinField(&m.X) the value is less than X Cannot be less than %v numbers MaxField(&m.X) the value is greater than X Cannot be greater than %v time BeforeField(&m.X) the value isn't before X Should be before %s time AfterField(&m.X) the value isn't after X Should be after %s comparable values EqualField(&m.X) the value isn't equal to X Should be equal to %s
  • The other field has the type of the configurator: string for str.Of, the number type for num.Of, time.Time for timex.Of.
  • The message has the location of the other field, by the location function of the validator: Should be after StartsAt, or Should be after starts_at with JSON paths.
  • The rule is skipped when the value or the value of the other field is absent, e.g. a field of a nil nested struct.
  • In Each the elements are compared with a field of the object: e.As(timex.Of).AfterField(&m.StartsAt).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "time"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/num"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/timex"
)

type Auction struct {
    StartsAt time.Time
    EndsAt   time.Time
    MinBid   int
    Bids     []int
    Password string
    Repeat   string
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Auction](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Auction], a *Auction) {
        b.Field(&a.EndsAt).As(timex.Of).AfterField(&a.StartsAt)
        b.Slice(&a.Bids).As(num.Slice).Each(func(bid *num.BaseConfigurator[int]) { bid.MinField(&a.MinBid) })
        b.Field(&a.Repeat).As(str.Of).EqualField(&a.Password)
    })

    start := time.Date(2026, 5, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
    auction := &Auction{
        StartsAt: start,
        EndsAt:   start.Add(-time.Hour),
        MinBid:   100,
        Bids:     []int{150, 90},
        Password: "secret",
        Repeat:   "Secret",
    }
    for _, err := range v.Validate(context.Background(), auction) {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
}

Output:

Should be after StartsAt (EndsAt: 2026-04-30 23:00:00 +0000 UTC)
Cannot be less than MinBid (Bids[1]: 90)
Should be equal to Password (Repeat: Secret)

For a comparison of several fields that doesn't fit one rule, use a struct custom rule.

docs.title: gin
docs.text:
The module github.com/insei/valigo/gin validates the requests of gin by valigo.

go get github.com/insei/valigo/gin@latest
  • vgin.New(v) is the binding.StructValidator of gin: set binding.Validator = vgin.New(v), and c.ShouldBindJSON and the other binding methods validate the requests by the rules of valigo. Slices are validated element by element, the location of an error has the index: [1].email.
  • gin doesn't pass the request to its validator, so these messages are in the default language. vgin.Validate(c, v, &req) validates with the languages of the Accept-Language header of the request.
  • The error is shared.Errors, get the errors by errors.As and write them, e.g. as problem details.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "errors"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "net/http/httptest"
    "strings"

    "github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
    "github.com/gin-gonic/gin/binding"
    "github.com/insei/fmap/v3"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    vgin "github.com/insei/valigo/gin"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/problem"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type SignUp struct {
    Email string `json:"email"`
    Name  string `json:"name"`
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New(valigo.WithFieldLocationNamingFn(func(f fmap.Field) string { return f.GetTagPath("json", false) }))
    valigo.Configure[SignUp](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[SignUp], s *SignUp) {
        b.Field(&s.Email).As(str.Of).Required().Email()
        b.Field(&s.Name).As(str.Of).Required().MaxRunes(16)
    })
    // the binding of gin validates by valigo, without the validation of its own tags
    binding.Validator = nil

    gin.SetMode(gin.ReleaseMode)
    r := gin.New()
    r.POST("/sign-up", func(c *gin.Context) {
        var req SignUp
        if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {
            c.Status(http.StatusBadRequest)
            return
        }
        if err := vgin.Validate(c, v, &req); err != nil {
            var errs shared.Errors
            if errors.As(err, &errs) {
                _ = problem.New(errs).Write(c.Writer)
                return
            }
        }
        c.Status(http.StatusCreated)
    })

    req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/sign-up", strings.NewReader(`{"email": "ann", "name": ""}`))
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    req.Header.Set("Accept-Language", "de")
    w := httptest.NewRecorder()
    r.ServeHTTP(w, req)
    fmt.Println(w.Code)
    fmt.Print(w.Body.String())
}

Output:

422
{"title":"Validation failed","status":422,"errors":[{"detail":"Muss eine E-Mail-Adresse sein","pointer":"#/email","location":"email","code":"string.email"},{"detail":"Muss ausgefüllt sein","pointer":"#/name","location":"name","code":"string.required"}]}

To validate by the binding methods instead, set binding.Validator = vgin.New(v): the messages are in the default language then.

docs.title: huma
docs.text:
The module github.com/insei/valigo/huma validates the inputs of huma operations by valigo. The errors are the error details of huma with its locations — body.email, query.limit, path.id — in the 422 response of huma, and the messages are translated to the languages of the Accept-Language header.

go get github.com/insei/valigo/huma@latest

import vhuma "github.com/insei/valigo/huma"

var validator = valigo.New(valigo.WithFieldLocationNamingFn(vhuma.Location))

func (i *CreateUserInput) Resolve(ctx huma.Context) []error {
    return vhuma.Resolve(ctx, validator, i)
}
  • vhuma.Location is the location function of the input structs of huma: the fields of Body are body and their JSON path, the parameters are their kind and name from the path, query, header, cookie and form tags.
  • vhuma.Resolve validates the input with the languages of the Accept-Language header and returns the error details of huma, huma calls Resolve of the input after it has parsed the request.
  • vhuma.Errors converts the errors of ValidateTyped to the error details of huma. The error details of huma have no codes, use problem when the clients need them.

huma validates the input by its JSON schema first, so the rules of valigo extend the schema: formats, rules on other fields, rules from data, translated messages.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "net/http/httptest"
    "strings"

    "github.com/danielgtaylor/huma/v2"
    "github.com/danielgtaylor/huma/v2/adapters/humago"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    vhuma "github.com/insei/valigo/huma"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/num"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type CreateUserInput struct {
    Limit int `query:"limit"`
    Body  struct {
        Email string   `json:"email"`
        Tags  []string `json:"tags"`
    }
}

var validator = valigo.New(valigo.WithFieldLocationNamingFn(vhuma.Location))

func init() {
    valigo.Configure[CreateUserInput](validator, func(b valigo.Configurator[CreateUserInput], i *CreateUserInput) {
        b.Field(&i.Limit).As(num.Of).Max(100)
        b.Field(&i.Body.Email).As(str.Of).Email()
        b.Slice(&i.Body.Tags).As(str.Slice).Each(func(tag *str.BaseConfigurator) { tag.Alphanumeric() })
    })
}

func (i *CreateUserInput) Resolve(ctx huma.Context) []error {
    return vhuma.Resolve(ctx, validator, i)
}

func main() {
    mux := http.NewServeMux()
    api := humago.New(mux, huma.DefaultConfig("Users", "1.0.0"))
    huma.Post(api, "/users", func(context.Context, *CreateUserInput) (*struct{}, error) { return nil, nil })

    r := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/users?limit=500", strings.NewReader(`{"email": "ann", "tags": ["go", "a b"]}`))
    r.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
    r.Header.Set("Accept-Language", "ru")
    w := httptest.NewRecorder()
    mux.ServeHTTP(w, r)

    var resp struct {
        Status int `json:"status"`
        Errors []struct {
            Location string `json:"location"`
            Message  string `json:"message"`
        } `json:"errors"`
    }
    _ = json.Unmarshal(w.Body.Bytes(), &resp)
    fmt.Println(resp.Status)
    for _, err := range resp.Errors {
        fmt.Println(err.Location, "-", err.Message)
    }
}

Output:

422
query.limit - Не может быть больше 100
body.email - Должно быть электронным адресом
body.tags[1] - Должно содержать только латинские буквы и цифры

docs.title: Maps
docs.text:
b.Map(&m.X) returns the configurator of a map[K]V field: the rules of the map itself, of its keys and of its values. The keys and the values are converted to the configurators of their types by As, like the elements of slices:

b.Map(&s.Labels).Required().MaxLen(10).
    EachKey(func(k *shared.Field[string]) { k.As(str.Of).Alphanumeric().MaxLen(32) }).
    EachValue(func(v *shared.Field[string]) { v.As(str.Of).MaxLen(64) })
b.Map(&s.Ports).EachValue(func(p *shared.Field[int]) { p.As(num.Of).AnyOfInterval(1, 65535) })

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Fails when Message Required() the map is absent or empty Should be fulfilled MinLen(n) the map has less than n elements Cannot contain less than %d elements MaxLen(n) the map has more than n elements Cannot contain more than %d elements EachKey(fn) — fn configures the rules of the keys EachValue(fn) — fn configures the rules of the values Custom(fn) fn returns errors, it gets the whole map your messages, see Custom rules When(fn) — the next rules are applied only if fn returns true for the map, a nil map for an absent one
  • The location of an error of a key or a value is Labels[key], the error value is the key or the value.
  • The order of a map is random, so the errors of the keys and the errors of the values are sorted by location.
  • The values of a map aren't addressable: Trim and other modifying rules change a copy, which is checked by the next rules, the map keeps the original value.
  • A nil map of a value field is present and empty, the map of a nil nested struct is absent.
  • Valid maps are validated without allocations, the copy of the checked key or value is pooled.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/num"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
)

type Service struct {
    Labels map[string]string
    Ports  map[string]int
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Service](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Service], s *Service) {
        b.Map(&s.Labels).Required().MaxLen(10).
            EachKey(func(k *shared.Field[string]) { k.As(str.Of).Alphanumeric() }).
            EachValue(func(v *shared.Field[string]) { v.As(str.Of).MaxLen(5) })
        b.Map(&s.Ports).EachValue(func(p *shared.Field[int]) { p.As(num.Of).AnyOfInterval(1, 65535) })
    })

    errs := v.Validate(context.Background(), &Service{
        Labels: map[string]string{"app": "valigo-api", "tier!": "web"},
        Ports:  map[string]int{"http": 80, "admin": 0},
    })
    for _, err := range errs {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
}

Output:

Should contain only letters and digits (Labels[tier!]: tier!)
Cannot be longer than 5 characters (Labels[app]: valigo-api)
Only interval[1 - 65535] is allowed (Ports[admin]: 0)

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
num.Of converts a numeric field to the number configurator, num.Ptr — a pointer to a numeric field. Supported types are int, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64, float32, float64 and named types based on them.

The arguments of the rules have the type of the field. Untyped constants fit any numeric type, a value of another type doesn't compile:

type Price int64

type Product struct {
    Stock    int
    Price    Price
    Rating   float32
    Discount *uint8
}

b.Field(&p.Stock).As(num.Of).Min(0)
b.Field(&p.Price).As(num.Of).AnyOfInterval(1, 1_000_000) // the arguments are Price
b.Field(&p.Rating).As(num.Of).Max(5)
b.Field(&p.Discount).As(num.Ptr).Max(90)                 // a nil Discount is skipped

var limit int32 = 10
b.Field(&p.Stock).As(num.Of).Max(limit) // doesn't compile: int32 isn't int
b.Field(&p.Discount).As(num.Of)         // doesn't compile: *uint8 isn't a number, use num.Ptr

Slices of numbers are converted by num.Slice: b.Slice(&p.Sizes).As(num.Slice).Each(func(e *num.BaseConfigurator[int]) { e.Min(1) }), see Slices.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: Rule Fails when Message Required() num.Of: the value is zero; num.Ptr: the value is absent Should be fulfilled Min(n) the value is less than n Cannot be less than %v Max(n) the value is greater than n Cannot be greater than %v MinField(&m.X), MaxField(&m.X) the value is less or greater than the value of the field X, see Rules on other fields Cannot be less than %v, Cannot be greater than %v AnyOf(values...) the value isn't one of values Only %v values is allowed AnyOfInterval(begin, end) the value is outside [begin, end], both ends are included Only interval[%v - %v] is allowed Latitude(), Longitude() the value is outside [-90, 90] / [-180, 180] Should be latitude, Should be longitude Custom(fn) fn returns errors your messages, see Custom rules When(fn) — the next rules are applied only if fn returns true, see Conditions

docs.title: Zero and absent
docs.text:
Zero is a valid value of a pointer: b.Field(&p.Discount).As(num.Ptr).Required() passes for a pointer to 0 and fails for nil. Use a pointer field when zero must be distinguished from "not set", e.g. in PATCH requests:

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/num"
)

type UpdateProduct struct {
    Stock *int
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[UpdateProduct](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[UpdateProduct], p *UpdateProduct) {
        b.Field(&p.Stock).As(num.Ptr).Min(0)
    })

    zero, negative := 0, -1
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &UpdateProduct{}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &UpdateProduct{Stock: &zero}))
    fmt.Println(v.Validate(context.Background(), &UpdateProduct{Stock: &negative}))
}

Output:

[]
[]
[Cannot be less than 0 (Stock: -1)]

docs.title: HTTP problem details
docs.text:
The problem package writes the validation errors as the problem details of RFC 9457 (it obsoletes RFC 7807): an application/problem+json response with the errors of the fields in the errors member.

v := valigo.New(valigo.WithErrorsTransformer(problem.Transformer()))

if errs := v.Validate(r.Context(), &req); errs != nil {
    problem.From(errs).Write(w) // 422 Unprocessable Content
    return
}
  • problem.Transformer(opts...) makes Validate return one error, the *problem.Details of all errors; problem.From(errs) gets it back, problem.New(errs) builds it from the errors of ValidateTyped.
  • Details.Write(w) writes the status and the JSON with the application/problem+json content type.
  • Every error of a field has the translated message detail, the JSON Pointer pointer of RFC 6901 (built from the location: tags[1] is #/tags/1), the location, and the code and params for the clients that translate the messages themselves.
  • Options: WithType (the URI of the problem type, about:blank when it is empty), WithTitle ("Validation failed" by default), WithStatus (422 by default), WithDetail.

Use JSON locations, so the pointers point to the fields of the request, see Errors.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "bytes"
    "encoding/json"
    "fmt"
    "net/http"
    "net/http/httptest"
    "strings"

    "github.com/insei/fmap/v3"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/problem"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/translator"
)

type SignUp struct {
    Email string   `json:"email"`
    Tags  []string `json:"tags"`
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New(
        valigo.WithFieldLocationNamingFn(func(f fmap.Field) string { return f.GetTagPath("json", false) }),
        valigo.WithErrorsTransformer(problem.Transformer(problem.WithType("https://example.com/problems/validation"))),
    )
    valigo.Configure[SignUp](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[SignUp], s *SignUp) {
        b.Field(&s.Email).As(str.Of).Required().Email()
        b.Slice(&s.Tags).As(str.Slice).MaxLen(2).Each(func(tag *str.BaseConfigurator) { tag.Alphanumeric() })
    })

    handler := translator.NewAcceptLanguageMiddleware()(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        var req SignUp
        if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
            http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
            return
        }
        if errs := v.Validate(r.Context(), &req); errs != nil {
            _ = problem.From(errs).Write(w)
            return
        }
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
    }))

    r := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/sign-up", strings.NewReader(`{"email": "ann", "tags": ["go", "a b", "api"]}`))
    r.Header.Set("Accept-Language", "ru")
    w := httptest.NewRecorder()
    handler.ServeHTTP(w, r)

    var body bytes.Buffer
    _ = json.Indent(&body, w.Body.Bytes(), "", "  ")
    fmt.Println(w.Code, w.Header().Get("Content-Type"))
    fmt.Print(body.String())
}

422 application/problem+json
{
  "type": "https://example.com/problems/validation",
  "title": "Validation failed",
  "status": 422,
  "errors": [
    {
      "detail": "Должно быть электронным адресом",
      "pointer": "#/email",
      "location": "email",
      "code": "string.email"
    },
    {
      "detail": "Не может содержать больше 2 элементов",
      "pointer": "#/tags",
      "location": "tags",
      "code": "slice.max_len",
      "params": {
        "max": 2
      }
    },
    {
      "detail": "Должно содержать только латинские буквы и цифры",
      "pointer": "#/tags/1",

      "code": "string.alphanumeric"
    }

The title isn't translated: set it by WithTitle, e.g. with a translator of your messages.

docs.title: Slices
docs.text:
b.Slice(&m.X) returns the configurator of a []E field with the rules of the slice itself. As converts it to a typed slice configurator, the rules of the slice stay available after the conversion:

Configurator Elements Rules on elements b.Slice(&m.X) any E Each with *shared.Field[E]: Check, Required, Modify, Custom, When, and As to convert the element .As(str.Slice) string, *string, named strings Each with the string configurator, Trim, Regexp, Email .As(num.Slice) numbers and named numbers Each with the number configurator .As(timex.Slice), .As(eq.Slice) times, comparable values Each with the time and the equality configurators, Unique of eq.Slice .As(vuuid.Slice) uuid.UUID, *uuid.UUID Each with the uuid configurator, AnyOf

A pointer to a slice, *[]E, is converted from its field: b.Field(&m.Tags).As(shared.SlicePtr).As(str.Slice), a nil pointer is absent.

docs.title: The slice and its elements
docs.text:
The rules of the configurator check the slice itself, the rules inside Each check every element:

Rule Fails when Message Required() the slice is absent or empty Should be fulfilled MinLen(n) the slice has less than n elements Cannot contain less than %d elements MaxLen(n) the slice has more than n elements Cannot contain more than %d elements Each(fn) — fn configures the rules of the elements

Trim, Regexp and Email of str.Slice and AnyOf of uuid.Slice are shortcuts for the same rules in Each. Any element of b.Slice is converted in Each too: e.As(num.Ptr).Max(100) for []*int.

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"

    "github.com/google/uuid"
    "github.com/insei/valigo"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/shared"
    "github.com/insei/valigo/str"
    vuuid "github.com/insei/valigo/uuid"
)

type Post struct {
    Tags       []string
    Editors    []*uuid.UUID
    Quantities []int
}

func main() {
    v := valigo.New()
    valigo.Configure[Post](v, func(b valigo.Configurator[Post], p *Post) {
        b.Slice(&p.Tags).As(str.Slice).Required().MaxLen(3).Each(func(tag *str.BaseConfigurator) {
            tag.Trim().Required().MaxLen(10)
        })
        b.Slice(&p.Editors).As(vuuid.Slice).Each(func(id *vuuid.BaseConfigurator) {
            id.Required()
        })
        b.Slice(&p.Quantities).Each(func(q *shared.Field[int]) {
            q.Check(func(v int) bool { return v > 0 }, "Should be positive")
        })
    })

    editor := uuid.MustParse("6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8")
    post := &Post{
        Tags:       []string{"go", "  ", "validation-library"},
        Editors:    []*uuid.UUID{&editor, nil},
        Quantities: []int{1, 0},
    }
    for _, err := range v.Validate(context.Background(), post) {
        fmt.Println(err)
    }
}

Output:

Should be fulfilled (Tags[1]: )
Cannot be longer than 10 characters (Tags[2]: validation-library)
Should be fulfilled (Editors[1]: <nil>)
Should be positive (Quantities[1]: 0)

The location of an element error has the index of the element, the errors of the slice itself have the location of the field. Nil elements of slices of pointers are absent: only Required fails on them.

docs.title: Custom and When
docs.text:
Custom and When of the slice configurators get the elements as shared.Elems[E], a view over []E and []*E without copying:

b.Slice(&p.Tags).As(str.Slice).Custom(func(ctx context.Context, h *shared.FieldCustomHelper, tags shared.Elems[string]) []shared.Error {
    seen := make(map[string]bool, tags.Len())
    for _, tag := range tags.All() { // tag is *string, nil for nil elements of []*string
        if tag != nil && seen[*tag] {
            return []shared.Error{h.ErrorT(ctx, *tag, "Tags should be unique")}
        }
        if tag != nil {
            seen[*tag] = true
        }
    }
    return nil
})

Len() returns the number of elements, At(i) the pointer to the element i, All() iterates over the indexes and the pointers.

docs.title: Slices of pointers
docs.text:
Slice works with the declared element type: for []*int the element is *int. Convert the element to check the pointed values, nil elements are absent then:

b.Slice(&p.Limits).Each(func(limit *shared.Field[*int]) {
    limit.As(num.Ptr).Required().Max(100)
})

docs.title: Strings
docs.text:
str.Of converts a string field, a *string field or a field of a named string type to the string configurator:

type Status string

type User struct {
    Name     string
    Nickname *string
    Status   Status
}

b.Field(&u.Name).As(str.Of).Trim().Required().MaxLen(64)
b.Field(&u.Nickname).As(str.Of).MinLen(3) // a nil Nickname is skipped
b.Field(&u.Status).As(str.Of).AnyOf("active", "blocked")

Slices of strings are converted by str.Slice, see Slices.

b.Slice(&u.Emails).As(str.Slice).MaxLen(3).Email()

docs.text:
